strings.lesson.channels.title: Images and RGB channels
strings.lesson.channels.summary: A colour pixel contains three numbers. Normal OpenCV capture uses B, G, R order. Splitting channels changes their organisation, not their values.
strings.lesson.channels.variables: x is the column and y the row; C is one selected channel. C₈ is an 8-bit value from 0 to 255; Cₙ is its normalised value from 0 to 1.
strings.lesson.channels.caution: Division by 255 applies to 8-bit data. It does not undo gamma encoding or produce a physical radiance measurement.
strings.lesson.channels.contract: Input bgr: a nonempty 8-bit, three-channel image. Outputs B, G, R: single-channel float32 images.
strings.lesson.difference.title: Signed frame difference
strings.lesson.difference.summary: Subtract the previous frame from the current one. Positive values mean a channel increased; negative values mean it decreased. Absolute difference discards the sign.
strings.lesson.difference.variables: C is the same channel at the same coordinate in two equally sized frames; t is the frame index. ΔC is a per-frame difference, not a derivative per second. Divide by the time interval Δt to estimate a time derivative.
strings.lesson.difference.caution: Convert to float first. uint8 arithmetic can clip negative results or wrap around. Lighting changes also change pixels; a difference alone does not prove motion.
strings.lesson.difference.contract: R and previousR: equally sized, single-channel float32 images.
strings.lesson.algebra.title: Channel algebra and weights
strings.lesson.algebra.summary: Build a new signal from channels. A linear combination retains direction, but channels can cancel each other. Euclidean magnitude measures total change size.
strings.lesson.algebra.variables: wR, wG, wB are chosen weights and may be negative. M is nonnegative. Weights in S are not the same as weights under the square root in a weighted norm.
strings.lesson.algebra.caution: S may exceed [0,1]. Clip only for display, not during calculation. This example uses dR − dG + 0.5·dB.
strings.lesson.algebra.contract: dR, dG, dB: equally sized float32 images.
strings.lesson.confidence.title: Derived confidence A
strings.lesson.confidence.summary: In SimpleMotocam, A is a derived quality weight. The initial model reduces confidence near black and clipped channels. This is our heuristic, not a built-in OpenCV confidence estimate.
strings.lesson.confidence.variables: R,G,B are normalised channels; m is the clipping-headroom margin. clip limits a value to the specified interval. M is the RGB change magnitude from the previous topic.
strings.lesson.confidence.caution: A is neither a probability of correctness nor RGBA opacity. A saturated colour can receive A = 0 even when an object is clearly visible. The model is replaceable.
strings.lesson.confidence.contract: Scalar example for one pixel; apply the same equation at every image coordinate. m must be in (0,0.5].
strings.lesson.filter.title: A filter kernel
strings.lesson.filter.summary: A linear filter combines neighbouring pixels using weights in a small matrix. Changing that matrix changes the filter mathematics. This example averages nine neighbouring pixels.
strings.lesson.filter.variables: K is a 3 × 3 kernel centred at (0,0); its weights sum to 1. X is the input channel and Y the output.
strings.lesson.filter.example: If the centre pixel is 1 and its eight neighbours are 0, the centre output is 1/9 ≈ 0.1111. A constant field remains constant.
strings.lesson.filter.caution: filter2D computes correlation: it does not flip the kernel. For convolution, flip both kernel axes. This symmetric kernel gives the same result either way. Border extension affects image-edge results.
strings.lesson.filter.contract: X: a single-channel float32 image. Python/C++/Java explicitly replicate border pixels; legacy C filter2D uses this border handling.
strings.lesson.gradient.title: Edges and spatial derivatives
strings.lesson.gradient.summary: Sobel estimates how quickly intensity changes along x and y. Combining the responses gives local change magnitude. This is not automatically an object outline.
strings.lesson.gradient.variables: ⋆ denotes correlation here. x increases rightward and y downward. The 1/8 factor normalises this 3 × 3 kernel; it is not the automatic default of every Sobel call.
strings.lesson.gradient.example: A vertical step from 0 to 1 gives |Gx| = 0.5, Gy = 0 and E = 0.5 at the two interior columns adjacent to the edge.
strings.lesson.gradient.caution: Compute derivatives in float because they are signed. Noise also produces edges; smoothing before differentiation changes the response.
strings.lesson.gradient.contract: X: a single-channel float32 image. This example uses kernel size 3 and BORDER_REPLICATE.
strings.lesson.threshold.title: Thresholds and binary masks
strings.lesson.threshold.summary: A threshold converts a continuous signal into a decision. It can turn change magnitude into a mask of pixels that exceed a selected limit.
strings.lesson.threshold.variables: M is the input signal and τ the threshold. B here denotes a binary mask, not the blue channel; the code uses the name mask.
strings.lesson.threshold.example: M = [0.1, 0.2, 0.3], τ = 0.2 → mask = [0, 0, 1]. Equality with the threshold is not sufficient.
strings.lesson.threshold.caution: A threshold does not identify an object. Its units must match the input signal. A 0/1 mask is not the same as a 0/255 display image.
strings.lesson.threshold.contract: M: a single-channel float32 image. The output mask is float32 with values 0 and 1.
strings.lesson.scale.title: From pixels to physical scale
strings.lesson.scale.summary: A reference of known length in the same plane and capture geometry lets us estimate local scale. This is a simple model, not general 3D calibration.
strings.lesson.scale.variables: Lref is the known length in mm, pref its pixel length, s the scale in mm/pixel, and p the measured pixel length. us and up are independent standard uncertainties of scale and detection.
strings.lesson.scale.example: A 10 mm reference spans 200 pixels: s = 0.05 mm/pixel. A 30 pixel object measures 1.5 mm. With us = 0.001 and up = 0.5, uL ≈ 0.0391 mm.
strings.lesson.scale.caution: Perspective, lens distortion and depth changes can invalidate a uniform scale. The uncertainty formula is a first-order approximation for independent variables; it does not include every systematic error.
strings.lesson.scale.contract: Scalar calculation with pref > 0. Application geometry and metrology are not implemented yet; this is a learning example.
